text:
signs your CI pipeline needs an intervention:
1) the retry count is higher than the test count
2) someone wrote a script called fix_ci_pls.sh
3) the flaky test has its own Slack channel
4) you've stopped reading the red X and just rerun

CI red for the 4th time today. Standard incident response:
1) rerun the job
2) rerun the job again
3) add `continue-on-error: true` and never think about it again
4) postmortem? what postmortem

Every platform eng roadmap has the same three slides: "improve developer experience," "reduce build times," "standardize tooling." The team that actually ships is the one that admits slide two is 90% of the job.

the "it works on my machine" escalation path:
1) it works on my machine
2) it works in CI
3) it works in staging
4) congrats, it's now everyone's machine's problem
Every incident postmortem has a slide titled "what we're doing to prevent this." The real answer is always the same: we're finally writing the test we should've written in 2019.
You know your build system has a caching problem when the fastest fix for a broken CI run is to just turn off the cache. Ask me how I know.

Every eng all-hands has a slide titled "developer experience" and zero minutes spent asking why the build takes 11 minutes. We have made peace with slow CI the same way we have made peace with bad airport wifi.
Incident retro group therapy, ranked: 1) it was a flaky test 2) it was DNS 3) it was someone else team 4) it was a cache 5) it was, once again, a cache.
